reader.requirement: At --std 85, an implementor-name-1 entry naming an external switch may associate its ON and/or OFF status with condition-names, in each of the four printed alternatives (mnemonic with ON then OFF, mnemonic with OFF then ON, ON with optional OFF, OFF with optional ON), and a switch-status condition naming one is true exactly when the switch is in that status (§1985:VI.6.3.1.4); a condition-name on a non-switch implementor-name is refused (SR2).

edition-consulted.switches: which SPECIAL-NAMES figure ranks the paragraph's clauses: below 2002 the 1985 figure's fixed sequence (switch entries before ALPHABET/SYMBOLIC/CLASS/CURRENCY/DECIMAL-POINT, else COBOL2987); at 2023 the 2023 figure, which does not rank them

reader.edition-search: grep of Edition/CobolVersion/Construct/DialectLevel over SpecialNamesBinder.cs, ImplementorNameEntry.cs, SetAlterBinder.cs (switch half), ConditionRenderer.cs Visit(BoundSwitchCondition), ImplementorNames.cs, SwitchStore.cs and the grammar rules implementorSwitchEntry/switchStatusPhrases/switchOnClause/switchOffClause: Edition.At only sets the diagnostic location; binding, condition rendering and the runtime are one arm at every edition. The only edition switch reached is the clause-order figure.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only the SPECIAL-NAMES clause order (a switch entry after CLASS is COBOL2987 at 85, accepted at 2023); the condition-name association and its truth value are the same code at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness exercises OFF-first with a mnemonic and ON-only without one, initial OFF and one SET; not exercised: the ON-then-OFF and OFF-only alternatives, an initial ON status from the external facility, NOT/compound/EVALUATE/PERFORM UNTIL uses, and the SR2 refusal

probes.printed: no environment: S1=OFF S1OFF=T S2=OFF S4=OFF U0=OFF BOTH-OFF EV-OFF I=3; with COBOL_SWITCH_1=ON COBOL_UPSI_0=1 COBOL_SWITCH_4=true COBOL_SWITCH_2=on: S1=ON S1OFF=F S2=ON S4=ON U0=ON BOTH-OFF EV-OFF I=3
probes.expected: each condition-name true exactly when its switch is in the named status (§1985:VI.6.3.1.4); all four 1985 alternatives accepted

probes.expected: refused: SR2, a condition-name cannot be associated with such an implementor-name

probes.printed: --std 85: COBOL2987 switch entry written after CLASS; --std 2023: runs, prints OFF

reader.notes: Every 1985 alternative binds through one grammar rule and one binder; the condition renders as ExternalSwitches.Get and the store reads COBOL_<SWITCH> once. The only edition branch on the path is the 1985 clause-order figure. Minor: a subscripted or qualified switch condition-name is refused with COBOL1639 'not defined', whose wording says the name has no declaration; the refusal itself is correct.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.4.5.2 format (four switch alternatives, STATUS/IS optional), VI.4.5.3 SR1-SR2, VI.4.5.4 GR1-GR3, VI.6.3.1.4. Probes at --std 85: E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-012/c9.cob (one switch across a nested program, a separately compiled program with its own SPECIAL-NAMES mnemonic and an OFF-only entry, and an ON-only entry with no mnemonic; with and without COBOL_SWITCH_3=ON): every program sees the one external status (M0 OFF/I0 OFF/I1 ON/M1 ON/O0 ON/M2 OFF/M3 OFF/O2 ON; env ON gives M0 ON/I0 ON). c10/c11 (same condition-name for two switches, and for ON and OFF of one switch): COBOL4250 refused. c12 (switch condition-name also an 88): unqualified reference refused COBOL1639 as ambiguous. c13 (SWITCH-1 named twice with two mnemonics): both mnemonics alter one switch, conditions correct. Class c: c15 later-edition reserved words RAISE/TYPEDEF/BASED as mnemonic and condition-names compile and run at 85 (refused COBOL0901 at 2023); c16/c17 1985-only reserved words EGI, SUB-QUEUE-1, SEGMENT-LIMIT refused COBOL0901 at 85. Edition sites: SetAlterBinder/SpecialNamesBinder grep shows ctx.Edition only as diagnostic sink; reserved-word table is the one other site and is right. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR2 (the text is in GR2); OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR1 (the text is in GR1).
